lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: thresholds: when to escalate

objective: Learners sort provided fictional situations into wait-and-monitor, get-help-soon, and get-help-now tiers, so they build the judgment to recognize escalation thresholds quickly rather than freezing when a real decision is needed.
scenario: Given a provided list of fictional situation examples spanning a range of urgency, the learner sorts each into one of three escalation tiers and explains the deciding factor for the two trickiest calls.
safetyNotes: All scenarios are provided and fictional; sorting them requires no disclosure of any real personal situation.
Anything involving immediate danger to health or safety always sorts into 'get help now,' with no exception.
materials: the provided list of fictional situation examples

tasks.directions: Before sorting, name what tips a situation from 'monitor' into 'act now' for you personally.

prompts.text: In your own words, what's the difference between a situation you'd just keep an eye on and one where you'd act immediately?

tasks.directions: Sort all the provided scenarios into the three escalation tiers.

prompts.text: I sorted every provided scenario into one of the three tiers.
Every scenario involving immediate danger to health or safety is in the 'get help now' tier.

tasks.directions: Explain the deciding factor for your two trickiest sorting calls.

prompts.text: Pick the two scenarios that were hardest to sort, and explain what specifically made the decision hard and how you resolved it.
If you genuinely couldn't tell which tier a real situation belonged in, which tier would you default to, and why is that the safer default?

remediation: If any immediate-danger scenario is sorted anywhere other than 'get help now,' this must be corrected before the lesson is considered complete — reteach the non-negotiable immediate-danger rule explicitly and have the learner re-sort those items only.
extension: Have the learner write one additional scenario of their own for each of the three tiers, explaining why each belongs where they placed it.
